headline: Mexican Peso Plunges 2.43% as US Federal Reserve Rate Hike Expectations Weigh
summary: The Mexican peso suffered its worst session in over a year, closing at 18.86 per dollar, as rising expectations that the US Federal Reserve could raise interest rates in December hit the currency.
why: Emerging market currencies like the Mexican peso are highly sensitive to shifts in US monetary policy expectations and interest rate differentials.

impacts.name: Mexican peso
impacts.why: Expectations of higher US interest rates strengthen the US dollar and prompt capital outflows from emerging market currencies.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Possibility of a US Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December triggered broad dollar strength, driving a 2.43% drop in the Mexican peso.
